proposal.title: Azure bounded-keyword RAG – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: an authenticated web app, sign-in with Entra ID, an API that enforces permissions and runs keyword retrieval, a catalog that stores document chunks and their ACLs, ingestion from Blob Storage, Azure OpenAI for generating answers, and monitoring. Assumptions: this is a small synthetic collection, the region is still to be chosen, and model access, quotas and region availability have not been verified. None of these Azure components has a native generator implementation here, so they are design intent that still needs engineering. Nothing is deployed.

data.label: Staff user (browser)
data.description: Person using the assistant in a browser. Client reference only, not provisioned.

data.label: Web app
data.description: Authenticated chat UI. Signs users in with Entra ID (auth code + PKCE) and shows answers with their source citations.

data.label: Identity
data.description: App registration issuing tokens with user and group claims. Whether we use an existing tenant or a new test tenant is still open.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: Validates the JWT, maps the user to groups, filters chunks by ACL, runs bounded keyword retrieval, calls the model and returns a cited answer, or declines if nothing permitted matches. Fails closed for unknown identities.

data.label: Document catalog + ACLs
data.description: Stores chunks, keywords, document revisions and explicit source ACLs. Read by the API; written only by ingestion.

data.label: Synthetic documents
data.description: Private container holding the synthetic UTF-8 documents and their permission metadata.

data.label: Ingestion
data.description: Chunks new or updated documents, extracts keywords and writes chunks with their ACLs to the catalog, using managed identity.

data.label: LLM
data.description: Chat model deployment that generates grounded answers. The model, regional availability and quota are not yet verified. Local tests use scripted responses instead.

data.label: Monitoring & audit
data.description: Logs requests, access denials and latency without storing document text.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If permissions are not enforced, an answer could leak a restricted document.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "keep all source permissions" and "identity enforcement".
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: answers use only chunks the signed-in user may read under the source ACLs, and unknown identities are denied.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Citations let users check answers. Declining when there is no source reduces made-up answers.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Answer questions over a small synthetic document collection with citations".
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: every answer cites the source documents it used, and the assistant declines to answer when no permitted source matches.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Region choice limits which models are available and decides where the data is stored.
requirementDrafts.basis: Inferred proposal; the user has not stated a country.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: deploy all data and model processing in an Azure region inside the required country (country still to be confirmed).

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message:
I wouldn't change the diagram to fix this one. The good news is the design is sound: the emulation found no failures and no wiring problems, and it was blocked before running any code. The blocker is on our side: this product can't yet generate Azure code for a sign-in-protected keyword search over documents, so all eight components report "implementation needed". Azure Blob Storage is the only one with a supported contract, so swapping or relabelling boxes would just hide that gap. To get this unblocked we need Azure versions of the web app, Entra sign-in, Functions search API, Cosmos catalog and blob-trigger ingestion, built by product engineering. The way to check that work is to rerun this same revision-2 scenario and see the gaps close.

Should we keep this Azure-only and wait for those Azure contracts? Or would you also like a side-by-side reference built on the supported AWS version of the same design, so we can run the permission and citation tests locally now? Either way, the scripted model only tests the flow, not answer quality.
